98.b42.box: Though it traveled a winding road, the concept of the one God that Melchizedek planted never went out in the West; it still flames anew today.
99.title: The Social Problems of Religion
99.b0.ask: “In a fast-changing society, how can religion lead the world by changing people, without being bound to institutions?”
99.b2.p: In Paper 98 we saw the path the Melchizedek teachings took in the West, through philosophy, cult, and church. Paper 99 now turns from history to the present and asks what relationship religion should have with society. Its answer is striking: religion achieves its highest social ministry when it has the least connection with the secular institutions of society.
99.b3.p: In the past, religion worked mainly to replace evil with good within the existing social order, and so, indirectly, it tended to keep that order in place. But religion should not be directly concerned either with creating new social orders or with preserving old ones. True religion opposes violence, but it does not oppose society’s intelligent efforts to adjust its institutions to new conditions. In the twentieth century, as conditions of living change so rapidly, religion too is called to adapt more quickly.
99.b4.p: So in a society that never stops changing, what should religion hold on to, and what should it let go?
99.b5.q: ⟦Q 99:6.1⟧It is far better to have a religion without a church than a church without religion.⟦/Q⟧
99.b8.p: Mechanical inventions and the spread of knowledge are reshaping civilization. The new social order will not settle down complacently for a thousand years; mankind must accept a procession of changes and readjustments. The social ship has left the sheltered bays of tradition for the high seas. In these dangerous times of transition, the chief social mission of religion is to stabilize the ideals of mankind.
99.b9.p: Religion has no new duties. But it is urgently called to act as a wise guide and experienced counselor. A godless humanitarianism is a noble gesture, yet only true religion can lastingly make one group respond to the needs and sufferings of others. Religion must not plunge directly into the secular work of social reconstruction, but it must keep restating its moral mandates and spiritual precepts in fresh language.
99.b10.q: ⟦Q 99:1.4⟧Religion must act as the cosmic salt which prevents the ferments of progression from destroying the cultural savor of civilization.⟦/Q⟧
99.b12.p: Institutional religion cannot lead the coming social reconstruction, because it has become an organic part of the very order that must be rebuilt. It is caught in a vicious circle: it cannot reconstruct society without first reconstructing itself, and it cannot reconstruct itself until society has been reconstructed. Only the real religion of personal spiritual experience can work creatively in this crisis.
99.b13.p: That is why religionists must act in society and politics as individuals, not as groups. The moment a religious group acts as a body outside religion, it becomes a political party or an economic organization. The church’s only proper stance is to teach peaceful evolution in place of violent revolution. The religion of living experience keeps ahead of social change, serving as a moral stabilizer and spiritual pilot.
99.b14.t: Becomes part of the established order
Bound by tradition and dogma, it struggles to adjust
A moral stabilizer and spiritual pilot
It glorifies the order of the past
The wisdom born of knowing God and striving to be like him
99.b16.p: Early Christianity was entirely free of civil and economic entanglements. The kingdom of heaven is neither a social nor an economic order; it is a spiritual brotherhood of God-knowing individuals. Religion influences society directly by spiritualizing each individual citizen, and indirectly as those citizens take part in many groups. The paper notes that the church’s long ministry to the unfortunate was good, but that an excess of false sentiment also held back the progress of civilization.
99.b17.p: Many reformers are moved by religious motives they do not recognize, but because these motives are never openly examined, they do not lead to self-correction. Religion is always in danger of being distorted, as when nations at war turn their religion into military propaganda. The paper names five things that keep religion free from unholy secular alliances.
99.b18.t: A philosophy that criticizes and corrects
Freedom from all social, economic, and political alliances
Growing insight and appreciation of cosmic values
99.b19.p: As a group, religionists should concern themselves with nothing but religion; yet any one of them, as an individual citizen, may become an outstanding leader of a reform movement. The business of religion is to create, sustain, and inspire cosmic loyalty in the individual.
99.b21.p: True religion gives new meaning to families, schools, and every human association, and it even exalts play and humor. Together with children, a living faith is the great unifier of family life. In the early twentieth century, family life — next to personal religious experience — suffers most from the passing of old loyalties. If religion is to help character grow, it must not be standardized, stereotyped, or formalized.
99.b22.p: It is what one believes, rather than what one knows, that determines conduct. Despite the achievements of science, countless people are anxious and unsettled, and they need the comfort of sound religion as never before. Man’s greatest spiritual danger is unfinished growth: leaving behind the religions of fear without yet grasping the religion of love. Real peace will come only when three partial approaches are brought into harmony.
99.b23.t: The spiritistic belief in a providential Deity
A revelatory presentation that portrays spirit, mind, and energy together
99.b25.p: Religion is a personal experience of knowing God as a Father, but because it leads to knowing man as a brother, it always has a social side. Religion begins as an inner adjustment and grows into social service. Jesus shattered tradition and dogma and called mankind to be perfect, even as the Father in heaven is perfect. Against the doctrine of man’s total depravity, Jesus sought to restore human dignity by declaring that all men are the children of God.
99.b26.q: ⟦Q 99:5.2⟧True religion is to know God as your Father and man as your brother.⟦/Q⟧
99.b27.p: Someday religionists will co-operate on the basis of shared ideals and purposes rather than theological beliefs. Goals rather than creeds should unite them. Jesus did not ask his followers to recite a formula; he asked them to gather and share the supper that remembers his bestowal life. And it is a great mistake to exalt Christ while requiring people to reject the God-knowing leaders of other peoples.
99.b29.p: Sectarianism is a disease of institutional religion, and dogmatism is an enslavement of the spiritual nature. Today’s religious turmoil may herald growth as well as destruction. Group religious activity does have a real purpose: to dramatize the loyalties of religion and to foster unselfish fellowship, family life, religious education, and group worship.
99.b30.p: But as religion becomes institutionalized, its power for good shrinks and its possibilities for evil multiply. Formal religion holds people back in their spiritual life instead of releasing them to serve as builders of the kingdom. Here are some of the dangers the paper lists.
99.b31.t: Serving the church instead of God
Sects, competing divisions, and religious castes appear
The saving message of the gospel is gradually lost
99.b33.p: Religious groups should stand aloof from secular activities, yet religion must not hinder the social co-ordination of human institutions. In social reconstruction, religion supplies a steady loyalty to a transcendent object, a goal beyond the immediate one. Religion inspires man to live courageously and joyfully on the earth; it joins patience with passion, insight with zeal, and ideals with energy.
99.b34.p: No one can wisely decide temporal issues or rise above selfishness without meditating in the presence of the sovereignty of God. Economic necessity ties us to reality, while personal religious experience brings us face to face with the eternal realities of cosmic citizenship.
99.b36.p: Paper 99 says that religion does not change society by putting institutions first. Institutional religion, as part of the order that needs rebuilding, cannot remake itself. But the living experience of knowing God as Father and man as brother changes people one by one, and those changed citizens become salt and light throughout society. The faster the times change, the more religion should stay true to its original mission — stabilizing human ideals and nurturing cosmic loyalty — rather than looking for new tasks. When it is united by goals rather than creeds, and serves God rather than the church, religion achieves its highest social ministry.
99.b37.t: In times of rapid change, religion is the cosmic salt that steadies our ideals
An institution that is part of the old order cannot rebuild itself
Religionists lead society as individual citizens, not as groups
The danger is leaving the religion of fear without grasping the religion of love
True religion is to know God as Father and man as brother
A religion without a church is far better than a church without religion
Religion inspires us to live courageously and joyfully through a transcendent loyalty
99.b39.box: Religion changes society not through institutions, but through the personal experience of knowing God as Father and man as brother.
100.title: Religion in Human Experience
100.b0.ask: “How does religion grow within a person until, at last, it shapes a balanced personality like that of Jesus?”
100.b2.p: In Paper 99 we saw that religion changes society not through institutions but through the experience of individuals. Paper 100 now steps inside that personal experience. The experience of dynamic religious living transforms an ordinary individual into a personality of idealistic power. And the progress of each person adds to the progress of all.
100.b3.p: Spiritual growth is stimulated by close association with other religionists. Love supplies the soil in which religion grows, and religion ennobles even the commonplace drudgery of daily living.
100.b4.p: So how does religion grow within us? And what kind of personality stands at the end of that growth?
100.b5.q: ⟦Q 100:1.4⟧The quickest way for a tadpole to become a frog is to live loyally each moment as a tadpole.⟦/Q⟧
100.b8.p: A child judges experience by how much pleasure it brings, but maturity grows as higher meanings take the place of personal pleasure. Some people are too busy to grow, and the chief obstacles to growth are prejudice and ignorance. Children should be given a chance to grow their own religious experience rather than having a ready-made adult experience forced on them. Real growth is measured not by products but by progress.
100.b9.p: Children are lastingly impressed not by precept or even example, but only by the loyalties of the adults around them. Religion cannot be bestowed, borrowed, or learned; it is a personal experience that grows as the quest for final values grows. Good habits help, but growth itself is always unconscious — a creative activity not in the subconscious, but on the superconscious levels of the mind.
100.b10.t: Solving problems in a spirit of worship
Sharing one’s spiritual life with one’s fellows
Avoiding selfishness and refusing to presume on divine mercy
Living as in the presence of God
100.b12.p: Spiritual development depends on keeping a living connection with true spiritual forces and on bearing fruit by passing on to others what we have received. Spiritual growth is first an awakening to needs, then a discernment of meanings, and then a discovery of values. Spirituality is at once a sign of how near we are to God and a measure of how useful we are to others, and it grows as selfishness is removed from our love.
100.b13.t: We become aware of our needs
A personality motivated by love, active in unselfish ministry, and devoted to wholehearted worship
100.b14.p: The goal of human self-realization should be spiritual, not material. Physical pleasures and human affections are ours to enjoy, but they are not the eternal foundations of an immortal personality. The God-knowing person has an inner bastion, the citadel of the spirit, which no flood of adversity can assail. So even when our fondest hopes crash, we can accept it as a redirection that clears the way for more noble and enduring realities.
100.b15.q: ⟦Q 100:2.7⟧Temporal securities are vulnerable, but spiritual sureties are impregnable.⟦/Q⟧
100.b17.p: Religion is not a technique for reaching a static, blissful peace of mind. It is an impulse that organizes the soul for active service — the enlistment of the whole self in loving God and serving man. Human likes and dislikes do not decide what is good and evil. We must distinguish between what is value and what has value; meaning is what experience adds to value, the appreciative awareness of values.
100.b18.t: What is experienced when realities are meaningfully related; never static
What experience adds to value; the appreciative consciousness of values
The union of the actual and the potential; the experiential realization of values
The growth of values, progress in meanings, and the realization of how the two are related
100.b19.p: Change that does not expand meaning is valueless — it is potential evil. We cannot cause growth, but we can supply the conditions for it. Love grows in the same way: it cannot be manufactured or purchased; it must grow. Man’s only contribution to growth is to mobilize all the powers of his personality — living faith.
100.b21.p: New meanings emerge only amid conflict. There can be no growth without psychic conflict and spiritual agitation. The great problem of religious living is to unify the powers of the soul under the rule of love, and the highest happiness is inseparable from spiritual progress. Jesus loved men so much because he placed such a high value on them.
100.b22.p: The paper illustrates this with a picture of a cave-dwelling ancestor. Seen alone — snarling, club raised — he hardly shows the dignity of man. But widen the picture: in front of him crouches a saber-toothed tiger, and behind him stand a woman and two children. Once we see his motive, the same man looks noble. Love is not born of willpower; it is born of understanding our neighbor’s motives.
100.b23.t: We sympathetically seek to discern the other person’s viewpoint and reasons
100.b24.q: ⟦Q 100:4.6⟧It is not so important to love all men today as it is that each day you learn to love one more human being.⟦/Q⟧
100.b26.p: The world is full of lost souls — not lost in the theological sense, but lost in direction. God-consciousness may grow naturally and gradually, or it may come suddenly at a moment of crisis, as it did for Paul and for Gautama Siddhartha. Most of the dramatic phenomena of conversion are psychological, but genuine spiritual experiences also occur, when the mind’s loyalty is complete and the indwelling spirit reaches down to the superconscious mind. Still, emotion alone is a false conversion; there must be faith as well as feeling.
100.b27.p: Rather than seeking conversion, the better way to approach the Adjuster is through living faith, sincere worship, and unselfish prayer. Habitual religious daydreaming is dangerous, and trancelike visionary states should never be cultivated as religious experience. Jesus never resorted to such methods to commune with the Father.
100.b28.t: Reflective worship and the prayer of thanksgiving
Toward the superconscious zone of spiritual contact
Fatigue, fasting, fear, anxiety, wild dancing, and the like
100.b30.p: Religion is not one function of life; it is a mode of living. The outstanding marks of all religion are unquestioning loyalty and wholehearted devotion to supreme values. Even if those values are base or false, the devotion is still religious — but a religion is genuine only to the extent that what it holds supreme is a real spiritual value.
100.b31.p: True religion is a living love, a life of service. It never leads to social isolation, and it does not destroy the sense of humor. It takes nothing away from life but adds new meaning to all of it. Its most amazing mark is a peace that passes all understanding. Evolutionary religion is a genuine experience, but revealed religion is excellent as well, because it adds divine wisdom.
100.b32.t: The same loyalty — the motives are very similar
100.b34.p: The average person cannot hope to reach the perfection of character Jesus attained, but every believer can develop a strong and unified personality along the lines of his. The unique feature of the Master’s personality was not so much its perfection as its symmetry — its exquisite, balanced unity. He was truly sincere, with nothing of the hypocrite in him. He lived the truth, even as he taught it.
100.b35.t: Surcharged with divine enthusiasm, but never fanatical
100.b36.p: Jesus was not a man of sorrows but a soul of gladness. His constant encouragement was “⟦Q 100:7.9|137:1.6|152:4.2⟧Be of good cheer,⟦/Q⟧” and his watchword was “Fear not.” He was indignant at sin, but his indignation never turned into anger at the sinner. Great because he was good, this perfectly unified personality still unifies human experience today, simplifies life, and transforms the mind.
100.b38.p: Paper 100 portrays religion not as a list of beliefs but as an experience that grows. That growth cannot be forced; it happens quietly, on the superconscious level, as we live each moment loyally. New meanings open as we pass through conflict, and tolerance, friendship, and love grow as we come to understand our neighbors’ motives. Living faith, worship, and unselfish prayer are a surer path than emotional conversions or mystical experiences. And at the end of that path stands the personality of Jesus, in which enthusiasm and restraint, courage and patience were exquisitely balanced. Whoever has him within becomes a new creature, day by day.
100.b39.t: Growth is unconscious; living loyally is the quickest way
Spiritual assurance is a citadel no adversity can overthrow
We cannot cause growth, but we can supply its conditions
Understanding our neighbor’s motives grows into tolerance, friendship, and love
Living faith and worship are better than emotion or visions
True religion is a living love, a life of service
Jesus’ personality lay less in perfection than in exquisite balance and unity
100.b41.box: Religion grows of itself in a life of loyalty, until at last it shapes a balanced and unified personality like that of Jesus.
101.title: The Real Nature of Religion
101.b0.ask: “How is religion sure of a God whom neither science nor philosophy can prove — and how does that assurance set a person free?”
101.b2.p: In Paper 100 we saw how religion grows within a person. Paper 101 goes one step further and asks what religion really is. As a human experience, religion ranges from the fear slavery of primitive man all the way to the sublime faith liberty of those who are conscious of sonship with the eternal God.
101.b3.p: Religion is the ancestor of ethics and morals, yet it is not merely a moral movement. There really is a true inner voice — the true light that lights every man — and this spirit leading is distinct from the ethical promptings of conscience. The assurance of religion goes beyond the reason of the mind, even beyond the logic of philosophy.
101.b4.p: So by what means is religion sure of God, and how is it related to science, philosophy, and revelation? And from what does that faith set us free?
101.b8.p: True religion is neither a system of philosophic belief proved by reason nor an ecstatic experience enjoyed only by mystics. It is not the product of reason, yet viewed from within it is altogether reasonable. It is the experience of eternal realities in time. The Thought Adjuster has no special mechanism of its own for self-expression; it works through the natural mechanism of the mortal mind.
101.b9.q: ⟦Q 101:1.3⟧It is your thoughts, not your feelings, that lead you Godward.⟦/Q⟧
101.b10.p: The divine spirit contacts us not through emotions but in the realm of our highest and most spiritualized thinking. So religion does not consist in finding new facts or unusual experiences; it consists in discovering new spiritual meanings in facts already well known. In the end this experience brings a person to conclude that he has no right not to believe in God. To doubt God would be to prove untrue to the deepest thing within us — the divine Adjuster.
101.b12.p: The fact of religion lies wholly in the religious experience of rational, average human beings. Reason, through science, may lead back through nature to a First Cause, but it takes faith to turn that First Cause into a God of salvation, and it takes revelation to validate that faith. Revelation affirms that the First Cause of science and the God of salvation of religion are one and the same Deity.
101.b13.t: It confirms the harmony of the other three approaches
101.b14.p: Nature can reveal only a God of nature, a God of motion; it gives no ground for believing in the survival of personality. The religious man who finds God in nature has already found him first in his own soul. Religion depends not on learning but on spiritual insight, so it is open alike to the learned and the unlearned. To those who share such an experience, no argument is needed; to those who do not, no argument could ever be convincing.
101.b15.t: The basic reasons for believing in God
The personal assurance, hope, and trust initiated by the indwelling Thought Adjuster
The Spirit of Truth, the bestowals of divine Sons, and the written revelations
101.b17.p: Religion is so vital that it persists without learning and survives even false cosmologies and philosophies. Faith-insight is the endowment of mind working with the Thought Adjuster; spiritual reason is the endowment of the Holy Spirit; and spiritual philosophy is the endowment of the Spirit of Truth. Together these make man a spirit personality in potential. The paper lists twelve ways in which genuine spiritual faith shows itself.
101.b18.t: Mark of genuine faith
Even in the face of
1. It makes ethics and morals progress
Adverse animal tendencies
2. It trusts in the goodness of God
Bitter disappointment and crushing defeat
3. It brings deep courage and confidence
Natural adversity and physical calamity
4. It shows inexplicable poise and tranquillity
Baffling diseases and acute suffering
5. It keeps the personality composed
Maltreatment and the rankest injustice
6. It trusts in ultimate victory
The cruelties of seemingly blind fate
7. It holds unswerving belief in God
All contrary demonstrations of logic
8. It believes in the soul’s survival
The delusions of false science and unsound philosophy
9. It lives and triumphs
The crushing overload of modern civilization
10. It keeps altruism alive
Selfishness, greed, and social conflict
11. It believes in universe unity and divine guidance
The presence of evil and sin
12. It goes right on worshiping God
Anything and everything: “⟦Q 101:3.16⟧Even though he slay me, yet will I serve him.⟦/Q⟧”
101.b19.p: So we know that a divine spirit dwells within man by three things: religious faith, revelation, and these extraordinary reactions to the material environment.
101.b21.p: Revelators are strictly forbidden to impart unearned or premature knowledge. So any cosmology presented with a revelation is soon outgrown, and later readers are tempted to throw out its religious truth because they find errors in its science. The paper says this of itself plainly: its historic facts and religious truths will stand, but many of its statements about the physical sciences will need revision within a few years. The cosmology of these revelations is not inspired.
101.b22.p: Truth is always a revelation: autorevelation when it comes through the Adjuster, and epochal revelation when it comes through celestial beings. In the last analysis, religion is to be judged by its fruits. Even though it is not inspired, a revealed cosmology has real value.
101.b23.t: It organizes known facts and observations
It recovers lost knowledge of the distant past
It supplies missing pieces in knowledge we have earned
It presents cosmic data so as to shed light on the spiritual teachings
101.b25.p: Revelation saves ages upon ages of time that would otherwise be spent sifting the errors of evolution from the truths of spirit. Science deals with facts, religion with values, and philosophy tries to unite the meanings of both. Religion appears in two phases, and it is part of the plan of the universe that evolutionary religion should be expanded by revelation.
101.b26.t: A mind derivative — the gift of the adjutant spirit
A spirit derivative — sponsored by the bestowal spirits
The assurance of faith and the confirmation of conscience
The assurance of faith plus the truth of a living experience
101.b27.p: Feeling and emotion always accompany religion, but they are not religion. As we progress through the morontia life, the assurance of truth increasingly replaces the assurance of faith; and in the spirit world, the assurance of pure spirit insight is added on top of both.
101.b29.p: Through every stage of religious experience, the Adjuster is the secret of the personal realization of the Supreme. Animals have knowledge, but only man has the capacity for wisdom, and truth opens to the mind that receives the Thought Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth. Michael himself lived under evolutionary religion until his baptism, and from his baptism to the cross under evolutionary and revealed religion combined.
101.b30.p: The teachings of Jesus were the first religion on Urantia to harmonize knowledge, wisdom, faith, truth, and love so fully that they gave peace, certainty, and the assurance of survival all at once. The faith of Jesus points to a sevenfold salvation.
101.b31.t: The truth shall set him free
By realizing brotherhood and discovering reality through service
By attaining the harmony of Havona and the perfection of Paradise
By release from the limitations of self-consciousness
By an eternal life of unending progression
By perfected oneness with Deity in and through the Supreme
101.b32.p: By taking hold of the faith of Jesus, we can foretaste in time the realities of eternity. The Father whom Jesus discovered, we too can discover — as we are, in this first life. Jesus was and is the new and living way to the Father.
101.b34.p: A personal philosophy of religion draws on both inner experience and outward circumstances — social status, education, temperament, vocation, even marriage. Sound conclusions require keen and honest thinking; moral cowards never reach high levels of philosophic thought. Religious philosophy evolves through four phases.
101.b35.t: Satisfied with slight attainments, letting well enough alone
Reaching logical intellect, but held in cultural bondage
Daring to think, act, and live honestly, loyally, and fearlessly
101.b36.p: The acid test of any religious philosophy is whether it distinguishes the material from the spiritual world while also recognizing their unity in striving and serving. A sound philosophy does not confuse the things of God with the things of Caesar.
101.b38.p: Accepting a teaching as true is only belief. Belief becomes faith when it actually shapes the way we live. Faith believes truth, admires beauty, and reverences goodness, but it worships God alone.
101.b39.t: Can rise up only in the heart of the individual
101.b40.p: Faith betrays itself when it denies realities or undermines intellectual honesty. Living faith does not foster bigotry or persecution, holds no unreasoning prejudice against the discoveries of science, and moves the religionist to live the golden rule heroically.
101.b42.p: No revelation is authentic if it fails to recognize the ethical duties fostered by earlier evolutionary religion; revelation always enlarges the ethical horizon. Primitive religion should be judged not by our standards but by the enlightenment and conscience of those who held it. The search for beauty and art become part of religion only when they are ethical and filled with high spiritual purpose.
101.b43.t: Projecting one’s estimate of moral values outward into the affairs of others
Adding spiritual values to moral values, so becoming conscious of divine reality
101.b44.p: Faith links moral consciousness to the spiritual concept of enduring reality. In this way religion becomes the avenue by which man escapes the limits of the temporal world for the realities of the eternal world.
101.b46.p: Neither the cause and effect of matter nor the continuity of ideas in the mind can show a person that his personality will survive. Logic and reason, even when exhausted, do not reveal the eternal truth of survival. Only in the spiritual sense is man a child of God, and by accepting the truth of God in faith he escapes the confines of material limitation. There can be no scientific or logical proof of divinity — but whoever wills to do the will of God shall comprehend the validity of spiritual values.
101.b47.p: The person set free by faith is no longer a slavish part of the mathematical cosmos but a liberated volitional son of the Universal Father. He no longer faces death alone or fights all nature with hopeless odds. God and all the divine hosts of the universe are on his side, and at last he sees the universe from within — from God’s viewpoint.
101.b48.q: ⟦Q 101:10.9⟧Even time itself becomes but the shadow of eternity cast by Paradise realities upon the moving panoply of space.⟦/Q⟧
101.b50.p: Paper 101 begins by making clear what religion is not. It is not a proven philosophy, not an ecstatic emotion, not intellectual assent to doctrine. It is the faith, trust, and assurance that arise when the indwelling spirit meets us in our highest thoughts. Science reaches as far as a First Cause, and philosophy as far as the attempt at unity; it is revelation that affirms this First Cause to be the God of salvation, and it is our own experience that validates revelation. The paper honestly admits that even its own cosmology will soon be outdated, and it says religion must be judged by its fruits: poise in suffering, unselfish love, and an unshakable trust in God. Through faith a person is freed from the bonds of matter, time, and self, and becomes a liberated son who sees the universe from God’s point of view.
101.b51.t: It is our highest thoughts, not our feelings, that lead us to God
Revelation affirms that science’s First Cause and the God of salvation are one
Genuine faith bears twelve fruits in every kind of adversity
Revealed cosmology is not inspired, yet it helps to clarify knowledge
Evolutionary religion of duty is destined to expand into revealed religion of love
The faith of Jesus is the new and living way to a sevenfold salvation
The courage to think fearlessly and honestly produces a high philosophy
True revelation always enlarges the ethical horizon
Faith turns a slave of the mathematical cosmos into a liberated son
101.b53.box: Religion is not proof but an assurance born of living experience with the indwelling spirit, and that faith makes a person a liberated son of God.
